Linters: cheap, fast checks that each catch one class of bug

02

A linter works like a spellchecker: a program, your files and a config

1 · The program

The linter itself

Spellchecker: the spellchecker

You install it once, like git or python. You run it; you never edit it.

on your machine iglint · shellcheck · yamllint
2 · The files

Your code, checked

Spellchecker: your document

The linter reads your files as text, never runs them, and flags anything against a rule.

in the repo projects/**/view.json · scripts/*.sh
3 · The config

Which rules are on

Spellchecker: your dictionary

One small file: the team's agreement on which rules to enforce and how strict.

in the repo: rules travel with the code iglint.toml · .yamllint.yml
03

The toolbelt, mapped to the files this repo tracks

Tool (the program)Runs on (the files)Catches
yamllintdocker-compose.yml · workflows · .yamllint.ymlYAML syntax and style: trailing spaces, truthy surprises (on:), indentation
shellcheckscripts/*.shNearly every shell bug ever made, like SC2086: an unquoted $VAR
actionlint.github/workflows/*.ymlWorkflow correctness: syntax, expression typing, stale runners and actions
iglinteverything under projects/Ignition-native: naming, poll rates, brittle references, Jython in views and scripts
scripts/validate.shevery *.json and code.py under projects/The green/red PR signal: valid JSON, parseable Python. Exit 0 green, 1 red
docker compose config -qdocker-compose.ymlCompose schema: undefined services, port-string typos, malformed env maps

iglint: the linter that reads a Perspective view

  1. view.jsonevery Perspective view under projects/
  2. iglintwalks the component tree, its expressions and the Python inside it
  3. Findingsper rule in iglint.toml, no running gateway needed
NAME001components PascalCaseerror · properties camelCasewarn · handlers kebab-casewarn · methods snake_caseerror
BIND004a floor on binding poll rates, 1000 ms in this lab: now(250) is a findingerror
VIEW018brittle traversal: .getSibling(), .getParent(), relative pathserror
BIND005do references actually resolve? Checks expressions and property bindings
SCR…the Python inside views and in the script library, parsed as Jython 2.7 like the gateway does

Kiln now points at a sibling tile by relative path, and someone renames BagsPerMin to Bags. The view still loads; the tile goes quietly blank.

VIEW018 · error

../../ traversal ties the binding to the view's structure: reorganise the tree and it breaks.

BIND005 · error

BagsPerMin doesn't resolve: there is no such component anymore.

BIND004 · error

The Clock polls at now(250), 4 times a second, under the 1000 ms floor. Multiply by every open session.

07

validate.sh checks that every project file parses; .yamllint.yml mutes a rule with a written reason

scripts/validate.sh
# every *.json under projects/ is valid JSON
# every code.py parses as Python 3
scripts/validate.sh
✓ all project files valid          # exit 0

# after a hand-edit leaves a trailing comma:
scripts/validate.sh
  ✗ invalid JSON: projects/lab-project/project.json
✗ validation failed                # exit 1
.yamllint.yml
rules:
  # Compose files have legitimately long
  # `environment:` lines (image tags, DB URLs,
  # JVM flags) that gain nothing from wrapping
  line-length: disable
08

pre-commit: the same linters, run at git commit

  1. git commiton your laptop
  2. scripts/git-hooksset as core.hooksPath by scripts/setup.sh
  3. .pre-commit-config.yamlof each lab the commit touches, on the staged files
  4. A hook failsthe commit is refused
# .pre-commit-config.yaml (ships in the lab)
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: iglint
        entry: iglint check labs/03-github-actions
        language: python
        additional_dependencies:  # pinned, like pip
          ["iglint==0.1.0"]
        files: ^labs/03-github-actions/.*\.(json|py)$
  # + yamllint, shellcheck, actionlint, pinned by rev:
# install the tool; there is no `pre-commit install`
uv pip install pre-commit
git config core.hooksPath     # → scripts/git-hooks
pre-commit run --all-files --config .pre-commit-config.yaml

# skip every hook for one commit
git commit --no-verify -am "..."

Workflow, jobs and steps: lab03-ci.yml drawn as boxes

workflow · .github/workflows/lab03-ci.ymlon: pull_request + push · permissions: contents: read
job: lintruns-on: ubuntu-latest

job: validateruns-on: ubuntu-latest

scripts/validate.shrun

The workflow is the file: it owns the triggers (on:), the permissions and a name. It contains jobs. Each declares runs-on, the machine it wants; jobs run in parallel by default. A job is a list of steps, in order: uses: calls a reusable action, run: runs the shell commands you ran locally.

12

Triggers: the on: block, with path filters

# .github/workflows/lab03-ci.yml (repo root)
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "labs/03-github-actions/projects/**"
      - "labs/03-github-actions/scripts/**"
      - "labs/03-github-actions/docker-compose.yml"
      - ".github/workflows/lab03-*.yml"
      - "labs/03-github-actions/.yamllint.yml"
      - "labs/03-github-actions/iglint.toml"
      - "labs/03-github-actions/.github/**"
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ["labs/03-github-actions/**", …]
pull_requeston open and on every push to the PR branch
push: [main]on every push or merge to main
paths:only when a listed file changes, configs included; patterns are repo-root-relative
workflow_dispatcha manual Run workflow button in the Actions tab
.github/workflows/at the repo root: the only place GitHub reads workflows
13

The finished lab03-ci.yml you rebuild in the exercise

name: Lab 03 · CI
on:
  pull_request:
    paths: ["labs/03-github-actions/projects/**", …]
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ["labs/03-github-actions/**", …]
permissions:
  contents: read              # least privilege
defaults:
  run:                        # run: steps start in the lab
    working-directory: labs/03-github-actions
jobs:
  lint:                       # job id = check name
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10       # not the 6 h default
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7          # each job starts empty
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"   # quoted, same as your venv
      - run: pip install yamllint==1.35.1 iglint==0.1.0
      - run: yamllint -c .yamllint.yml . ../../.github/workflows/lab03-*.yml
      - uses: raven-actions/actionlint@v2   # + with: lab03-*.yml
      - run: shellcheck scripts/*.sh        # apt-get install first
      - run: iglint check --output-format github .  # PR annotations
      - run: docker compose config -q
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - run: scripts/validate.sh
# set the finished file aside,
# start from a skeleton with TODOs
scripts/prepare-part2.sh

# when you're done: compare your
# build with the reference
git diff --no-index \
  .github/ci-reference.yml \
  ../../.github/workflows/lab03-ci.yml
14

Permissions, secrets and variables: least privilege for workflow credentials

permissions: contents: read

The workflow may read the repo (all checkout needs) and nothing else: no pushing, no issues, no releases. The default grant is broader than a lint job needs. Human access is untouched.

Secrets

Encrypted at rest, injected on demand, and masked as *** in logs. In the We-do we add one, echo it, and watch GitHub censor it live.

Variables

The unencrypted sibling: fine for a gateway URL, never for a password. If it would hurt in a screenshot, it's a secret.

# create a repo secret from the terminal
gh secret set EXAMPLE_SECRET --body "hunter2" \
  -R "$(gh repo set-default --view)"

# read it in a step; GitHub masks the value
      - run: echo "leak? ${{ secrets.EXAMPLE_SECRET }}"
# log: leak? ***
15

Protect main with a ruleset that requires lint and validate

Where
Settings › Rules › Rulesets › New branch ruleset
Name
protect-main · Enforcement: Active
Bypass list
empty (the rules bind admins too)
Target branches
Include default branch
  • Restrict deletions (main can't be deleted)
  • Require a pull request before merging · Required approvals: 0 (solo: no self-approval)
  • Require status checks to pass · add lint and validate
  • Block force pushes (no rewriting history)
  • Restrict updates stays off: it blocks PR merges too

From "please run the linters" to "you cannot merge until they pass".

One interaction to knowA required check whose workflow a paths: filter kept from starting never reports: the PR hangs on Expected. Two slides on is the fix.
A team contractWho decides what's blocking, and who fixes CI when it flakes? A check the team routinely overrides trains everyone to ignore red. Required reviews compose with it: human judgement and machine verification, in one ruleset.
16

Classic branch protection vs rulesets: the lab uses a ruleset

Classic branch protectionRuleset (what the lab uses)
WhereSettings › Branches › Add ruleSettings › Rules › Rulesets › New branch ruleset
AdminsExempt unless you also tick Do not allow bypassing the above settings: your direct push landsBound by every rule unless on the bypass list. Empty list: nobody gets around it, you included
ApprovalsRequire a pull request can pre-tick Require approvals: 1; alone you can never mergeYou set Required approvals: 0 for a solo fork, 1 or more for a team
TargetsOne branch-name pattern per rulePatterns, or Include default branch; rulesets stack on one branch
Switch offDelete the ruleEnforcement Disabled, or delete the ruleset
17

A README-only PR is blocked by the required checks, and a no-op twin workflow unblocks it

Only lab03-ci.yml

  1. PR changes only README.mda file the checks don't read
  2. lab03-ci.yml doesn't startits paths: filter skips the PR
  3. lint and validate never reportno workflow, no check
  4. Merge blockedthe PR waits on Expected forever

Plus lab03-ci-noop.yml

  1. PR changes only README.mda file the checks don't read
  2. lab03-ci-noop.yml startsits filter is the opposite one
  3. Jobs lint and validate passeach just runs an echo
  4. Merge allowedthe required names reported green
18

Build the no-op twin with paths: and ! negations

# .github/workflows/lab03-ci-noop.yml
name: Lab 03 · CI (no-op twin)
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "labs/03-github-actions/**"             # this lab's files...
      - "!labs/03-github-actions/projects/**"   # ...minus what
      - "!labs/03-github-actions/scripts/**"    # lab03-ci.yml checks
      - "!labs/03-github-actions/docker-compose.yml"
      - "!labs/03-github-actions/.yamllint.yml"
      - "!labs/03-github-actions/iglint.toml"
      - "!labs/03-github-actions/.github/**"
permissions: {}
jobs:
  lint:                     # same job ids = same check names
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "No lint-relevant files changed."
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "No validate-relevant files changed."

Self-hosted runners: when CI must reach a gateway behind your firewall

19

A self-hosted runner polls GitHub outbound, so nothing opens inbound

GitHub's cloud

Actions servicequeues jobs, stores logs
GitHub-hosted runners (ubuntu-latest)fine for lint and validate: no plant access needed
outbound poll
firewall / VPN
no inbound

Your network: plant or customer site

Self-hosted runnerpolls outbound "any jobs for me?", runs them, returns the logs
Ignition gatewaysthe deploy target GitHub-hosted can never reach
PLC network · historian DB · internal artifact registry

When you need one

Network isolation, the big one for Ignition: the gateway sits behind a firewall or customer VPN. Also compliance or data residency, real hardware, cost at very high volume.

When you don't

Everything in today's lab: lint and validate run on a standard image. A runner host is a machine you now own, patch and monitor.

20

The one rule for self-hosted runners, and the guardrails

Never attach a self-hosted runner to a public repo that accepts fork PRs: a malicious PR runs its code inside your network.

Ephemeraldestroyed after every job: nothing left behind
Private repostrusted contributors, approval for first-timers
Isolatedown subnet, only the outbound access it needs
No prod credentialsshort-lived tokens per job
Bareonly the tools you install on it
For Ignitiona build host that can reach the gateway, not the gateway server
21

Register an ephemeral runner in Docker, route one job to it, tear it down

# your repo, detected from the clone
REPO=$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner)

# short-lived registration token (expires in ~1 h)
RUNNER_TOKEN=$(gh api -X POST \
  "repos/$REPO/actions/runners/registration-token" --jq .token)

# one container = one runner
docker run -d --rm --name lab03-runner \
  -e REPO_URL="https://github.com/$REPO" \
  -e RUNNER_TOKEN="$RUNNER_TOKEN" \
  -e LABELS="self-hosted,local-lab03" \
  -e EPHEMERAL=true \
  myoung34/github-runner:latest
# EPHEMERAL: one job, then it deregisters and exits

docker logs -f lab03-runner   # "Listening for Jobs"
# .github/workflows/lab03-runner-demo.yml
on: workflow_dispatch
jobs:
  hello:
    runs-on: [self-hosted, local-lab03]  # the labels
    steps:
      - run: echo "ran on $(hostname)"

# run it; the job's output is in the run log
gh workflow run lab03-runner-demo.yml
gh run list --workflow lab03-runner-demo.yml --limit 1
gh run view <run-id> --log | grep "ran on"

# tear down
docker rm -f lab03-runner
